## How to use this

The code from Lecture 21, run, with the numbers it produces, and the exercises
solved.

. . .

The draws are random, so your last decimal place may differ from mine, more so
if you ran extra random code in between. Anything beyond that is worth asking
about.

::: {.notes}
Posted after class so nobody is left wondering whether their answer was right.
:::

## Setting up {.smaller}

```{r}
library(bbmle)

base <- "https://github.com/bmaitner/biometry_course/raw/refs/heads/main/data/class_examples/"
occ <- read.csv(paste0(base, "bobwhite_occupancy.csv"))
counts <- read.csv(paste0(base, "bobwhite_counts.csv"))

m_occ <- mle2(n_occupied ~ dbinom(size = n_routes, prob = plogis(a + b * elapsed)),
              start = list(a = 2, b = -0.05), data = occ)
coef(m_occ)
```

With the course package installed, `bobwhite_occupancy` and `bobwhite_counts`
give the same tables.

## The plug-in corners {.smaller}

```{r}
ci <- confint(m_occ)
corners <- expand.grid(a = ci["a", ], b = ci["b", ])
corners$occ_2019 <- plogis(corners$a + 22 * corners$b)
corners
cov2cor(vcov(m_occ))
```

Two of the corners go against the correlation of $a$ and $b$, so the data rule
them out.

## The recipe: occupancy in 2019 {.smaller}

```{r}
set.seed(21)
draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(1000, mu = coef(m_occ), Sigma = vcov(m_occ))
cor(draws)

occ19 <- plogis(draws[, "a"] + 22 * draws[, "b"])
quantile(occ19, c(0.025, 0.975))
```

## Your turn: how much was lost? {.smaller}

```{r}
occ97 <- plogis(draws[, "a"])
drop <- occ97 - occ19
quantile(drop, c(0.025, 0.975))
```

Occupancy fell by about 22 percentage points between 1997 and 2019, and the data
are consistent with a drop of anywhere from about 15 to 28.

## Two other ways {.smaller}

Rewrite the model so occupancy in 2019 is a parameter:

```{r}
occ$from2019 <- occ$elapsed - 22
m_2019 <- mle2(n_occupied ~ dbinom(size = n_routes, prob = plogis(a + b * from2019)),
               start = list(a = 1, b = -0.05), data = occ)
plogis(confint(m_2019, parm = "a"))
```

The delta method, for the curious:

```{r}
g <- function(th){ plogis(th[1] + 22 * th[2]) }
est <- g(coef(m_occ))
slopes <- sapply(1:2, function(i){
  th <- coef(m_occ)
  th[i] <- th[i] + 1e-6
  (g(th) - est) / 1e-6
})
se <- sqrt(drop(t(slopes) %*% vcov(m_occ) %*% slopes))
est + c(-1.96, 1.96) * se
```

## The band {.smaller}

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3.2
years <- occ$elapsed
curves <- matrix(NA, nrow = 1000, ncol = length(years))
for (i in 1:1000) {
  curves[i, ] <- plogis(draws[i, "a"] + draws[i, "b"] * years)
}
lower <- apply(curves, 2, quantile, 0.025)
upper <- apply(curves, 2, quantile, 0.975)

obs <- occ$n_occupied / occ$n_routes
plot(occ$year, obs, pch = 16, ylim = c(0.5, 1),
     xlab = "year", ylab = "fraction of routes occupied")
lines(occ$year, plogis(coef(m_occ)["a"] + coef(m_occ)["b"] * years), lwd = 2)
lines(occ$year, lower, lty = 2)
lines(occ$year, upper, lty = 2)
```

## The prediction interval {.smaller}

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3
preds <- matrix(NA, nrow = 1000, ncol = length(years))
for (i in 1:1000) {
  p_i <- plogis(draws[i, "a"] + draws[i, "b"] * years)
  preds[i, ] <- rbinom(length(years), size = occ$n_routes, prob = p_i) / occ$n_routes
}
pred_lower <- apply(preds, 2, quantile, 0.025)
pred_upper <- apply(preds, 2, quantile, 0.975)

plot(occ$year, obs, pch = 16, ylim = c(0.5, 1),
     xlab = "year", ylab = "fraction of routes occupied")
lines(occ$year, lower, lty = 2)
lines(occ$year, upper, lty = 2)
lines(occ$year, pred_lower, lty = 3, col = "red")
lines(occ$year, pred_upper, lty = 3, col = "red")
c(inside_confidence = sum(obs >= lower & obs <= upper),
  inside_prediction = sum(obs >= pred_lower & obs <= pred_upper))
```

## Counts and development {.smaller}

```{r}
m_nb <- mle2(count ~ dnbinom(mu = exp(log_mu0 + b * frac_built), size = exp(log_k)),
             start = list(log_mu0 = 2.5, b = -3, log_k = 0), data = counts)
coef(m_nb)

set.seed(22)
draws_nb <- MASS::mvrnorm(1000, mu = coef(m_nb), Sigma = vcov(m_nb))

log(2) / -coef(m_nb)["b"]
log(2) / -confint(m_nb)["b", ]
quantile(log(2) / -draws_nb[, "b"], c(0.025, 0.975))    # the recipe agrees
```

## Your turn: the band for development {.smaller}

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3
built <- seq(0, 0.5, by = 0.01)
counts_curves <- matrix(NA, nrow = 1000, ncol = length(built))
for (i in 1:1000) {
  counts_curves[i, ] <- exp(draws_nb[i, "log_mu0"] + draws_nb[i, "b"] * built)
}
nb_lower <- apply(counts_curves, 2, quantile, 0.025)
nb_upper <- apply(counts_curves, 2, quantile, 0.975)

plot(counts$frac_built, counts$count, col = "grey", ylim = c(0, 40),
     xlab = "fraction developed", ylab = "bobwhite counted")
lines(built, exp(coef(m_nb)["log_mu0"] + coef(m_nb)["b"] * built), lwd = 2)
lines(built, nb_lower, lty = 2)
lines(built, nb_upper, lty = 2)
c(nb_lower[21], nb_upper[21])
```

## Your turn: one route {.smaller}

```{r}
mu_20 <- exp(draws_nb[, "log_mu0"] + draws_nb[, "b"] * 0.2)
quantile(mu_20, c(0.025, 0.975))

one_route <- rnbinom(1000, mu = mu_20, size = exp(draws_nb[, "log_k"]))
quantile(one_route, c(0.025, 0.975))
```

We know the average route at 20% developed to within about a bird, but a single
route could turn up anywhere from none to around twenty. Both are true: the
first is a confidence interval, the second a prediction interval.
